hash_method: sha256 of the UTF-8 body after the frontmatter, stripped. design/check_gates.py does not exist in this repository, so the hash was computed with that rule. It is the round-3 text all three gates read.
status: Three rounds run, the cap. Not approved. Round 3 still has a blocker and major findings, and the critic named first-party alternatives the doc never evaluated, so per design-first the problem is upstream and the doc goes back to the owner instead of a fourth round.
scope_changes: After round 1 the original doc was split: the Command topic and the live call became issue drafts in design/issues/voice-agents-next/ (0003, 0004).

After round 2 the owner set voice approval aside (design/issues/voice-agents-next/voice-approvals.md) and chose tap approvals through the PermissionRequest hook, a button per question option, redacted cards, and a reply keyboard.

checks_run.B1-B5: PermissionRequest hook: allow and deny work, input carries the full tool_input, the prompt shows while the hook waits, a late hook decision closes it, a terminal answer wins
checks_run.B6: the hook keeps running after a terminal answer, and the transcript grew at the answer (one 5-second Bash run only)
checks_run.C: UserPromptSubmit additionalContext produced a final Spoken: line
checks_run.E: allow with updatedInput.answers answered an AskUserQuestion
checks_run.A: a digit selects on a numbered dialog with no Enter

findings: 16 gaps, chiefly event delivery, spoken-reply identity, Telegram cannot be hands-free, command session lifecycle, call-server auth. Led to the split.

Blockers: confirm not tied to the read-back prompt, auto-send approving a prompt, the call confirming itself, no call-server auth, the command session hijacking the vault conversation. Found the PermissionRequest hook.
9 blocking questions, folded into the split and the round-2 doc
17 mechanics gaps: write order, unmute verb, hook lifetime after a terminal answer, the bell fallback, event-log lifecycle
11 blocking: read-back speech queueing, bell fallback owner, seq and cursor, footer pattern, allowed() reuse, session key versus topic

Blocker: a spoken read-back does not let the ear verify a shell command. Major: the hook also fires for questions and plans, request files outlive prompts, the approval round trip does not fit, Codex and OpenCode have dialogs, typed control words bypass the read-back, unmute announces everything, new data class. Led to setting voice approval aside.
Detail gaps: session key to topic mapping, module import path, helper mute status, kill-switch writer, S job schema, spelled-out numbers in the hold

8 blocking: the PreToolUse question card fires before the request exists, trim changes the inode and skips events, done files lack message ids, no mute-status verb, no kill-switch writer, no store for partial answers, Send, /say, Edit replies and Enter can still approve an open prompt, prompt cards silent in hands-free topics
Blocker: atomic-rewrite trim gives a new inode, which resets the cursor and drops the spoken line of the trimming stop
Major: transcript growth is not a reliable 'answered elsewhere' signal (async rows such as away_summary, parallel tool results); bind the request to its tool_use_id instead
Major: two cards per question, since PreToolUse runs before PermissionRequest
Major: question handling while the hook waits was never verified

Major: done files lack message ids; import path and hook/bridge version skew; cards skip the session allowlist; journal text through Bash cards; auto-send can type into a shell after a crash; /say, Control Send, Send and Enter still type into an open prompt; prompt cards silent in hands-free; helper cannot report mute state

Minor: auto mode auto-denies unattended safety prompts after 120 s; act only on tools a card can describe; session key sanitisation breaks topic lookup; nested headless runs; kill switch has no writer
Alternatives not evaluated: Claude Code 2.1.310 ships a channel permission relay that dismisses a prompt answered elsewhere, and Remote Control (/rc). Both give request ids and cancellation natively.

open: Evaluate Claude Code's first-party Remote Control and channel permission relay before redesigning prompt cards
